candidates.original_title: The Political Relevance of Irrelevant Events
candidates.description: The outcome of a college football game affects presidential approval, university satisfaction, and mood.
candidates.citation_sentence: We seek to replicate one of these studies (i.e., Busby et al., 2017).
candidates.notes: Replication used different teams (Alabama and Clemson) and a different championship game (2016 vs. 2015), making it a close extension rather than a direct replication. The replication found effects for the losing team (Clemson) on presidential approval, university satisfaction, and mood, but not for the winning team (Alabama) and not for other outcome variables; authors explicitly call it a partial replication.
